document: EudraLex Vol.4 Part I Chapter 4 Documentation (in force version)
version_or_date: Revision dated January 2011; in operation since 30 June 2011 (issued together with Annex 11 rev. 2011)
notes: Current binding text as of 2026-09-27 per available sources; primary URL https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/104b3eb8-81a7-4858-9419-cb06562adb66_en?filename=chapter4_01-2011_en.pdf . Direct fetch of EC/EMA/PIC/S sites was blocked by this environment's network policy, so clause content was cross-checked through web-search result summaries plus prior knowledge; clause numbers 4.1-4.32 follow the 2011 text.

document: EudraLex Vol.4 Part I Chapter 5 Production (in force version)
version_or_date: Revision published August 2014; in operation since 1 March 2015
notes: Changes vs. earlier text: QRM/toxicological-assessment based prevention of cross-contamination (links to Chapter 3 and EMA HBEL guideline) and strengthened supplier qualification / supply-chain traceability for starting materials; added clause on reporting manufacturing constraints that could cause supply shortages. Primary URL https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/4a1fdb4f-6f6f-49c4-b264-8056e5bbe078_en . Numbering used here (5.1-5.71) is from recollection of the 2014 text and was only partly confirmed via search summaries; see per-line verified flags.

requirement: An approved master formula must exist for every product AND every batch size. It identifies the product via a code linked to its specification, states dosage form, strength and batch size, lists every starting material with its quantity (calling out any ingredient that is removed during processing), and gives the expected final yield with acceptance limits plus relevant intermediate yields.
system_implications: Master recipe entity keyed by product code + batch size (or an explicitly approved set of discrete sizes); no ad-hoc scaling at batch creation. Bill of materials with quantity per batch and a 'removed during processing' flag (tablets: granulation water/ethanol; injectables: WFI removed by lyophilisation, process gases, declared overages). Mandatory yield targets with lower/upper limits at final and configured intermediate stages. Only masters in Approved/Effective status can be instantiated.
verification_test: Try to create a batch for an unapproved batch size -> rejected. Try to approve a master lacking yield limits or spec-linked product code -> rejected. Flagged evaporating ingredient is listed in the BOM but excluded from theoretical output mass used in yield calculation.

requirement: Processing instructions must cover four themes: (1) setting - location, principal equipment and how critical equipment is readied (including sterilisation where relevant), directly or by reference; (2) readiness - a pre-start confirmation that the workstation holds nothing left from earlier work and that equipment is clean and usable; (3) method and control - ordered steps covering material checks, pre-treatment, order of addition and critical parameters such as time and temperature, plus in-process tests with their limits; (4) holding and safety - bulk storage needs where relevant (container, labelling, special conditions) and any particular precautions.
system_implications: Master step model must carry: room/area and equipment class; equipment-preparation prerequisites evaluated at run time (clean status and clean-hold expiry, calibration due date, assembly check, sterilisation status and sterile-hold expiry for injectables); a mandatory pre-start clearance step; ordered steps with CPP set-points and ranges; IPC definitions with limits; bulk hold definitions (container type, label, storage condition, maximum hold time); precaution text shown and acknowledged at the step. Tablets: granulation end-point, drying temperature/LOD, compression force/hardness. Injectables: SIP/autoclave cycle, filter integrity, bulk solution hold time.
verification_test: Master approval blocked if a CPP has no range or an IPC has no limit. At execution, selecting equipment whose clean or sterile status has expired, or whose calibration is overdue, blocks the step. Bulk hold exceeding maximum time raises an exception.

requirement: Approved packaging instructions are required per product, pack size and pack type, covering (directly or by reference): (1) what is packed - product identity with bulk and finished batch numbers, dosage form, strength and pack content by count, weight or volume; (2) what it is packed with - a complete component list with quantities, sizes, types and specification codes, plus, where appropriate, specimens of printed items showing where batch number and expiry go; (3) readiness - line clearance and inspection of area and equipment before starting, and other precautions; (4) method and control - a description of the operation including significant ancillary operations and equipment, and in-process checks with sampling instructions and acceptance limits.
system_implications: Packaging master keyed by product + pack size + pack type, versioned and approved separately from the processing master. Component BOM with item codes linked to approved specifications and artwork versions; artwork specimen image stored with coding/expiry print zones; mandatory line-clearance checklist template; operation steps with equipment classes; IPC plans with sample size, frequency and limits. Batch record must hold both the bulk batch number consumed and the finished-goods batch number. Tablets: blister/bottle counts, desiccant, leaflet. Injectables: vial/ampoule labels, cartons, tamper evidence, serialization data carriers.
verification_test: Approving a packaging master where a printed component has no linked artwork specimen or no coding zone is blocked. Starting a packaging order is blocked until the clearance checklist is complete. Packaging record shows bulk lot and finished lot linkage.

requirement: A processing record is kept for every batch, generated from the currently approved formula and instructions. Its content falls into four groups: (1) who and when - product and batch identity, dates and times of start, key stages and finish, who performed each significant step and who checked it where relevant, and sign-off by the person responsible for processing; (2) what went in - lot or QC number and actual weighed quantity of each starting material, including any recovered or reprocessed material; (3) how it ran - notable events, main equipment used, in-process results with the tester's identity, and yields at relevant stages; (4) what went wrong - notes on special problems, with signed authorisation for any departure from the instructions.
system_implications: Batch record instance is generated only from the effective master version and stamps that version ID. Automatic server-time stamps at step start/stop and stage milestones. Per-step performer e-signature plus configurable second-person verification. Material consumption captured by lot scan and balance integration (actual weight, not keyed-in theoretical), with a distinct flag and source-batch reference for recovered/reprocessed material. Equipment ID captured per step. IPC results entered against limits with performer ID. Stage and final yields auto-calculated. Deviations linked to the step with authorised signature. Final 'production approval' signature role gates hand-over to QA/QP review.
verification_test: Execute a test batch; confirm master version is recorded, every significant step shows performer and time, weighed lots and actual quantities are present, yields computed, and that production approval cannot be applied while any step is incomplete or any deviation unsigned.

requirement: Where a process is validated and under continuous monitoring and control, automatically generated batch reports may be restricted to a compliance summary together with reports of exceptions and out-of-specification data.
system_implications: Support review-by-exception: a per-batch compliance summary and an exception report listing every out-of-range value, alarm, override, manual entry, correction, deviation and audit-trail change. Only steps configured (under change control, referencing the validation) as validated and continuously monitored may use summary-only reporting; full underlying data is still captured, retained and viewable on drill-down.
verification_test: Run a batch with one injected out-of-limit reading and one manual correction; both must appear in the exception report; data for in-range steps is available on drill-down; attempt to enable summary-only reporting on a step without a validation reference is refused.

requirement: A packaging record is kept for each batch or part-batch packed, derived from the packaging instructions. Content groups: (1) who and when - product and batch identity, dates and times, performers of significant steps and checkers where relevant, and sign-off by the person responsible for packaging; (2) conformity - identity and conformity checks against the instructions, in-process results, and details of the operations with the equipment and lines used; (3) evidence - where possible, specimens of the printed components actually used, including batch coding, expiry and any overprint; (4) exceptions - special problems or unusual events, with signed authorisation of departures; (5) accountability - quantities and identity of printed components and bulk issued, used, destroyed or returned, and the quantity of product obtained, enough to reconcile.
system_implications: Packaging record supports part-batch (sub-lot) records linked to one bulk lot. Captures line ID and equipment IDs, IPC results, and an attached specimen of printed material (scanned sample or vision-system image of the actual coded item). Reconciliation table per printed component and bulk: issued, used, destroyed, returned, plus finished units, samples and rejects. Final approval signature by packaging-responsible role.
verification_test: Complete a packaging run; record contains line ID, IPCs, a specimen image of a coded label/carton, full reconciliation table, and approval; approval is blocked while reconciliation fields are empty (unless the documented electronic-control exemption in EU4-07 is active).

requirement: The quantity reconciliation data for printed components and bulk may be left out of the packaging record only where robust electronic controls operate during packaging and this is justified.
system_implications: Reconciliation is ON by default for every packaging master. Turning it off for a component requires a controlled configuration change that names the electronic control relied on (e.g. 100% code/vision verification with verified reject, roll-fed labels with splice detection, serialization aggregation), references its validation, and is approved by QA. The record then shows the justification reference instead of counts. Serialized injectable/tablet packs: reconcile commissioned vs. decommissioned vs. shipped serial numbers as the electronic equivalent.
verification_test: Attempt to disable reconciliation without a QA-approved justification record -> blocked. With an approved justification, packaging record displays the justification ID; audit trail records who enabled it and when.

requirement: Documentation rules apply whatever the medium (paper, electronic, photographic). Each type of document must be defined and adhered to. Complex systems must be understood, documented, validated and adequately controlled. For hybrid (part paper, part electronic) and single-medium systems alike, the firm must describe how masters, official copies, data processing and the resulting records relate to one another and how each is controlled; electronic templates, forms and masters need appropriate controls; and record integrity must be protected for the entire retention period.
system_implications: eBMR must declare, per record type, which is the official (master) record: electronic record, printout, or combination. Hybrid points (e.g. printed labels, paper chart recorder output, instrument printouts, paper deviation forms) must be formally mapped with a documented linkage (scan attached as true copy, ID cross-reference). Templates/forms in the system are version-controlled, approved and locked. System is validated (Annex 11) and its configuration controlled.
verification_test: Documentation review: a record-type register exists showing official medium per record type. Test that editing a released template is impossible without a new version and approval. Test that a paper attachment carries a unique ID, is linked to the batch and step, and is reviewed as part of the record.

requirement: Documents must be carefully designed, drafted, reviewed and issued, and be consistent with the marketing authorisation and product specification file. Producing working copies from masters must not be able to introduce errors. Documents holding instructions must be approved, signed and dated by authorised people, have clear content and a unique identifier, and state when they take effect; they should be laid out logically, easy to check, and written as directives.
system_implications: Batch record instances are generated programmatically from the approved master (no copy/retype). Master recipe workflow: author -> reviewer(s) -> approver with e-signatures, unique document ID + version, and an effective-from date after which it becomes executable. Optional MA cross-check field (dossier reference / variation number) on the master. Instructions rendered as numbered imperative steps.
verification_test: Confirm the batch record content equals the master content (hash/field comparison) for a generated batch. A master with approval but future effective date cannot be instantiated before that date. Unapproved draft cannot be instantiated.

requirement: Quality-system documents must be reviewed periodically and kept current, and once a document is revised there must be a mechanism that prevents the superseded version from being used by mistake.
system_implications: Masters carry a periodic review due date with alerts; upon approval of a new version the prior version is automatically retired for new batches. Defined rule for batches in progress when a master changes (continue on old version with justification or migrate under change control) and the record shows which version governed each step. Printed forms or labels from superseded versions are invalidated (version/ID printed on every output).
verification_test: Approve v2 of a master; attempt to start a new batch on v1 -> blocked. Check in-flight batch behaviour follows the configured rule and is audit-trailed. Overdue periodic review is flagged on a dashboard.

requirement: Controlled documents themselves should not be handwritten; where data must be entered, adequate space must be provided, and any handwritten entries must be clear, legible and indelible.
system_implications: Every data point in the master has a defined, typed entry field (unit, precision, allowed range or list) so free-text is the exception. Where paper remains (hybrid printouts, emergency paper fallback forms), the printed form is generated from the approved master with enough space for each entry, carries a unique form ID, and is later reconciled into the electronic record. No handwritten master instructions.
verification_test: Master editor refuses a data-entry step without a field definition. Printed fallback form shows batch ID, form ID/page x of y and dedicated fields for every entry; issued fallback forms are counted and all returned forms reconciled.

requirement: Records must be made or completed when each action is performed, so that every significant manufacturing activity can be traced.
system_implications: Timestamps come from a synchronised server clock, never from a user-editable field. Steps are signed at completion; late entries are allowed only via a 'late entry' path that records actual time of activity, time of entry and a mandatory reason, and are flagged for review. Batch-level genealogy links materials, equipment, rooms, people and steps.
verification_test: Attempt to backdate a timestamp -> not possible. Enter a step 2 h after its planned window via late-entry path: record shows both times, reason and a review flag that appears in the exception report.

requirement: Any change to a recorded entry must be signed and dated by the person making it, the original value must remain readable, and a reason must be recorded where appropriate.
system_implications: Corrections never overwrite: the system keeps original value, new value, who, when (server time) and a mandatory reason (pick-list plus free text) in a secure audit trail. Corrections to GMP-relevant data after step sign-off require re-signature and, for critical data (weights, IPC results, CPPs, yields), a second-person or QA approval. Correction history is shown inline in the batch record view and in the exception report.
verification_test: Correct a weighed quantity after signing: original remains visible, reason required, correction appears in the audit trail and exception report, and step is re-signed. Attempt a correction without reason -> blocked. Direct DB update is detectable (audit trail/hash check).

requirement: The firm must define which record belongs to each manufacturing activity and where it is kept, and must have secure controls, validated where appropriate, that keep records intact throughout their retention period.
system_implications: Record-type register inside the system (or linked SOP) mapping each activity to its record and storage location (eBMR DB, archive, attached external systems such as SCADA/historian, LIMS, weighing). Integrity controls: role-based write access, audit trail, backup/restore tested, checksums on archived records, readable-format migration plan. Archive/export produces complete human-readable batch record with metadata and audit trail.
verification_test: Restore a batch record from backup/archive and compare against checksum; record opens with all data, signatures and audit trail intact. Register lists location of every record type referenced by the master.

requirement: Batch documentation must be retained for the longer of: one year beyond the batch expiry date, or at least five years after QP certification of the batch. For investigational medicinal product batches the minimum is five years after the last clinical trial using the batch is completed or formally stopped. Product-specific legislation (e.g. ATMPs) may demand longer periods.
system_implications: Retention engine computes a retention-until date per batch = max(expiry + 1 year, QP certification date + 5 years), stored with the record and recomputed if expiry is extended/changed; IMP batches use a separate rule tied to trial end dates entered by QA; configurable overrides for longer national or product-type rules. Purge/delete of batch records is impossible before that date and requires QA-approved, audit-trailed disposition afterwards. Retention applies to the full record including audit trails, attachments and linked data (e.g. historian extracts).
verification_test: Batch with 24-month shelf life certified 2026-01-10: retention date = 2031-01-10 (5 y after certification exceeds expiry+1 y). Batch with 60-month shelf life: expiry + 1 y governs. Attempt deletion before retention date -> refused and logged.

requirement: Other documents are retained according to the activity they support. Critical documentation, including raw data supporting the marketing authorisation (e.g. validation or stability data), is kept while the authorisation is valid; it may be retired only when superseded by a complete new data set and with a documented justification, and raw data behind process validation must be kept at least as long as the records of every batch released on the basis of that validation.
system_implications: Masters, master versions, recipe change history, and any validation-linked configuration (e.g. the validated state that justifies review-by-exception) are retained at least as long as any batch record that relied on them. Link each batch to the master version and validation references so retention of those objects is automatically extended while dependent batches are retained.
verification_test: Attempt to archive-delete a master version still referenced by a batch within retention -> blocked with a dependency message.

requirement: Written procedures must govern release and rejection of materials and products, especially QP certification of finished product. The QP must be able to see every record, and a mechanism must flag notable observations and any modification of critical data.
system_implications: QP/QA review workspace that exposes the complete batch record plus linked deviations, change controls, lab results and audit trails. Automatic flags for special observations (comments, events, deviations) and for any post-entry change to data classified as critical, so the reviewer sees them without searching. Release status workflow: quarantine -> production approved -> QA reviewed -> QP certified / rejected, each with e-signature.
verification_test: Change a critical data point after completion and add an operator comment: both surface as flags in the QP review screen; QP certification is blocked until each flag is acknowledged.

requirement: Logbooks are required for major or critical production equipment, analytical testing and areas where product is processed, recording in time order the use, calibration, maintenance, cleaning or repair, with dates and the identity of who performed the work.
system_implications: Electronic equipment and room logbooks that are automatically populated from batch execution (usage start/stop with batch and product ID, cleaning events) and from maintenance/calibration modules; entries are chronological and immutable (corrections per EU4-13). Batch step checks equipment/room status from the logbook (last product, clean status, calibration due). Injectables: also autoclave/SIP cycles, filter integrity tests, isolator/RABS decontamination. Tablets: compression machine tooling (punch/die sets) usage.
verification_test: Run two batches on the same granulator/filling line; logbook shows both usages and the intervening cleaning in chronological order with performer IDs; attempt to insert a back-dated logbook entry without the late-entry path fails.

document: EudraLex Vol.4 Part I Chapter 4 Documentation - draft revision (joint EMA GMDP IWG / PIC/S)
version_or_date: Consultation draft published 7 July 2025; comments closed 7 October 2025
status: draft (not final as of latest source found; no final publication located up to 2026-09-27)
notes: Published together with draft Annex 11 rev. and new draft Annex 22 (AI). Draft grows from 9 to about 17 pages and from 32 to about 85 clauses; roughly half rewritten. Main themes: data governance system embedded in the PQS (draft 4.10-4.18), six-stage data lifecycle (draft 4.12), two-axis data criticality / data risk assessment (draft 4.13), ALCOA++ codified (adds traceable), metadata and audit trails as part of records, hybrid systems explicitly recognised but to be defined and risk-controlled, dedicated section on signatures (identity and meaning of each signature, signature policy, e-signatures permanently linked for the record lifetime), glossary (true/certified/verified copy, raw vs derived data, metadata, hybrid system). Batch-record content lists and batch retention periods appear carried over. Final text was expected mid-2026 with a 6-12 month transition; a secondary source (hero.ie) states it was still a draft on 30 July 2026 and EudraLex still listed the 2011 text. Draft URL: https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/fa336a6e-753b-46fc-b53b-9178bacd8878_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_consultation_guideline_en.pdf ; consultation page: https://health.ec.europa.eu/consultations/stakeholders-consultation-eudralex-volume-4-good-manufacturing-practice-guidelines-chapter-4-annex_en . Primary pages could not be opened from this environment; status and content confirmed only through multiple secondary summaries.

requirement: (Draft, not yet binding) Firms must run a data governance system inside the PQS that manages integrity of all GMP data in any format across its whole lifecycle, with controls scaled to risk and supported by suitable expertise and defined ownership.
system_implications: eBMR ships with a data-governance configuration layer: data inventory of every record type and field with an assigned data owner/system owner; documented data flows to/from integrated systems (scales, MES/SCADA, historian, LIMS, ERP, serialization); role model with segregation of duties; periodic data-integrity review reports (user access, audit-trail review status, failed log-ins, configuration changes).
verification_test: Export the data inventory and verify every master field has an owner and criticality; generate the periodic DI review report for a test period and confirm it lists access changes, config changes and open audit-trail reviews.

requirement: (Draft) Controls must cover each lifecycle stage: creation/recording; processing of raw data into reported (derived) data such that the processing can be reconstructed; review/verification; decisions based on the data; retention, archiving and retrieval; and controlled retirement or destruction.
system_implications: Store raw captured values (e.g. individual balance readings, each IPC tablet weight, each fill-weight check, sensor readings) alongside derived results (means, RSD, yields, reconciliation %) together with the formula/version used, so any derived number can be recalculated. Review step status per record. Archive and retrieve functions with readability checks. End-of-retention destruction only via QA-approved workflow with a destruction certificate.
verification_test: For a completed batch, recompute yield and IPC averages from stored raw values and compare with the reported derived values; change of a formula version is traceable to the batches it affected; destruction without approval is blocked.

requirement: (Draft) Controls are to be based on two assessments: how critical the data is (its influence on decisions and product quality) and how exposed it is (opportunity for change or deletion and the likelihood that this would be detected).
system_implications: Each master data field carries a criticality attribute (e.g. critical / major / minor) and each capture method a risk attribute (automatic interface vs. manual entry vs. transcription from paper). Rules engine derives controls from the pair: second-person verification, mandatory reason codes, correction approval level, audit-trail review sampling, exception-report inclusion. Manual entry of critical data is flagged and, where an interface exists, disallowed by default.
verification_test: Configure a critical field captured manually: system enforces witness verification and puts every entry in the exception report; the same field captured via validated interface does not require witnessing but every manual override is flagged.

requirement: (Draft) All GMP records, paper or electronic, are expected to meet the extended data integrity attributes: attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring, available and traceable.
system_implications: Map each attribute to a feature: attributable = unique user IDs, no shared accounts, device/instrument ID on captured data; legible = human-readable rendering of every record incl. audit trail; contemporaneous = server time stamps and late-entry flag; original = first-capture value retained, interfaces store source files; accurate = validated calculations, range checks; complete = batch cannot close with open steps, all repeats/aborted attempts kept; consistent = sequence enforcement and time-order checks; enduring/available = archive and retrieval across retention; traceable = end-to-end audit trail and genealogy.
verification_test: Trace matrix from each ALCOA++ attribute to at least one validated test case; e.g. a repeated IPC measurement keeps both values (complete) and shows who/when (attributable/contemporaneous).

clause: draft metadata/audit trail provisions and glossary
requirement: (Draft) Records include the metadata and audit trail needed to reconstruct their history (who did what, when and why), whatever the medium; raw data (first capture) is defined and must be kept together with the derived data and the steps that produced it.
system_implications: Audit trail is always on, cannot be disabled or edited by any role, and records create/modify/delete/sign events with user, server time, old value, new value and reason. Metadata (units, instrument ID, method/formula version, recipe version, time zone) stored with each value and exported with the record. Audit-trail review of GMP-critical entries is a defined step in batch record review before release, with reviewer signature.
verification_test: Attempt to deactivate audit trail as admin -> impossible. Modify a critical value and confirm full audit entry. QA review cannot be completed while the audit-trail review task for the batch is open.

requirement: (Draft) Hybrid paper/electronic arrangements are acknowledged but must be clearly defined, with the interfaces and data flows between formats validated and risk-controlled; commentators report that printing electronic records to sign them by hand, and parallel paper-plus-electronic signatures, are treated as higher risk and to be avoided where possible.
system_implications: Design for fully electronic execution and signature; no built-in 'print to sign' path for GMP steps. Where paper is unavoidable (e.g. supplier CoA, thermal printouts, downtime forms), the system defines which is the original, captures a verified scan with metadata, links it to the step, and requires reconciliation of issued vs. returned paper forms. Business-continuity (downtime) procedure with controlled paper forms generated from the master and later data re-entry with second-person check.
verification_test: Search configuration for any step whose signature is paper-only -> none. Simulate downtime: printed forms bear unique IDs, are reconciled, and re-entered data are flagged as transcribed and verified.

clause: draft section on signatures in GMP documentation
requirement: (Draft) The purpose and control of signatures are spelled out: each signature must make clear who signed and what the signature means (e.g. performed, checked, reviewed, approved); a company signature policy is expected; electronic signatures are fully recognised but must be binding, traceable and stay permanently linked to the signed record for its lifetime.
system_implications: Signature manifestation on screen and in every rendered/exported record: full printed name, user ID, date-time with time zone, and signature meaning chosen from a controlled list configured per step. Signing requires re-authentication (e.g. ID + password or equivalent) at each signing event. Signature is cryptographically or logically bound to the exact record content/version; any later change invalidates or requires re-signing. Signature policy configured in system: which roles may sign which meanings, and a rule that performer and verifier must be different users.
verification_test: Sign a step: rendered record shows name, date-time, meaning. Attempt verifier signature with the same user as performer -> refused. Edit data after signing -> signature marked invalid / re-sign required. Copy/paste of a signature to another record is impossible.

clause: draft retention/copies provisions and glossary (true, certified, verified copy)
requirement: (Draft) Where the storage medium will not last for the retention period, verified true copies must be made; copies used in place of originals must preserve content and meaning (including metadata) and the verification must be documented; backup, restore and archiving must keep records readable and accessible for the full retention time.
system_implications: True-copy function: scans/exports carry source ID, checksum, capture metadata and a verifier e-signature confirming completeness and legibility; for electronic-to-electronic copies, include audit trail and metadata. Typical eBMR uses: thermal balance/pH/checkweigher printouts (fade), paper chart recorder output (e.g. autoclave/lyophiliser charts for injectables), label specimens. Archive format and migration plan preserve readability; periodic restore tests.
verification_test: Scan a thermal printout via the true-copy function: result carries checksum, verifier signature and link to step; alteration of the file breaks checksum validation. Annual restore test of an archived batch record opens with metadata and audit trail.

requirement: Yield checks and quantity reconciliations are to be performed as needed to show there are no discrepancies beyond acceptable limits; any significant departure from the expected yield must be recorded and investigated.
system_implications: Master defines yield/reconciliation checkpoints with theoretical basis, formula and alert/action limits. At each checkpoint the system calculates the result from captured quantities (inputs, outputs, samples, rejects, waste, residues) and blocks progression past a hard limit until a deviation is opened, linked and (as configured) approved. Results within limits are recorded; out-of-limit results appear in the exception report and hold batch disposition. Tablets: granule yield after drying/milling, compressed tablet count vs. theoretical, coating weight gain. Injectables: compounded volume vs. theoretical, filled units vs. theoretical, lyophilised vials, visual-inspection rejects.
verification_test: Enter quantities that produce a yield below the action limit: system forces deviation creation before the next step and flags the batch; a yield inside limits proceeds without deviation. Recalculation from raw quantities matches the displayed yield.

requirement: Before a processing operation starts, it must be confirmed that the area and equipment are clean and hold no materials, products, residues or paperwork unrelated to the operation about to begin.
system_implications: Mandatory processing-area clearance step at the start of each processing stage (and after interruptions/changeovers) using a master-defined checklist; the system verifies electronically what it can (previous batch closed in the room/equipment logbook, equipment clean status and clean-hold time valid, no open material lots assigned to the room) and requires signed confirmation of physical checks. Configurable independent verification by a second person. Stage cannot start until clearance is signed.
verification_test: Attempt to start granulation/compounding while the room logbook shows the prior batch not cleared or equipment clean-hold expired -> blocked. After signed clearance (and verifier signature if configured), the step unlocks and both signatures appear in the batch record.

requirement: Different products may only be handled in the same room at the same time, or back-to-back, if this has been shown to create no risk of mix-up or cross-contamination.
system_implications: Room/area occupancy control: the system tracks which batch/product occupies each room and refuses to start a second product in a room already occupied, unless the room is configured (under QA approval) as segregated for concurrent work with a documented risk assessment reference. Consecutive product use requires completed cleaning and clearance before the room status returns to available.
verification_test: Start batch A (product X) in room R; attempt to start batch B (product Y) in room R -> blocked with message. After batch A closes and cleaning + clearance are recorded, batch B can start.

requirement: During processing, every material, bulk container, major equipment item and, where appropriate, room must carry a label or other identification showing the product or material, strength where relevant, batch number and, where applicable, the production stage. Labels must be unambiguous, easy to read and follow the company's standard layout; colours signalling status (such as quarantine, approved, rejected or cleaned) are recommended as an extra aid.
system_implications: System generates and prints status/identity labels from batch data in approved templates (product, strength, batch, stage, container n of N, gross/tare/net, status, date/time, user) with a barcode/2D code; room and equipment status displays (e.g. 'In use - product/batch/stage', 'Cleaned - valid until', 'To be cleaned'). Scanning of container and equipment labels at each step verifies identity and status, replacing reliance on visual checks. Status changes (quarantine -> released -> rejected) update electronic status and require relabel/reprint with audit trail.
verification_test: Weigh a material into a container: label shows all required fields and a scannable code. Scan a container labelled for a different batch or stage at the next step -> rejected. Equipment status screen changes from 'In use' to 'To be cleaned' at batch end.

requirement: Deviating from instructions or procedures is to be kept to a minimum; when a deviation does happen, a competent person must give written approval, with Quality Control involved when relevant.
system_implications: Recipe enforcement prevents undocumented departures (sequence, limits, material identity). Any intentional departure (e.g. parameter outside range, step skipped, alternative equipment) is only possible through an in-line deviation/exception form that captures description and impact and requires e-signature approval by a role flagged as competent for that deviation class; QA/QC approval is mandatory for classes configured as quality-impacting. Deviation ID is linked to the step and appears in the batch record and exception report; batch release is blocked while linked deviations are open.
verification_test: Try to skip a mandatory step -> blocked unless a deviation is raised and approved by an authorised role. Operator cannot self-approve. Release blocked with an open deviation.

requirement: Dispensing of starting materials is restricted to designated staff working to a written procedure, so that the right material in the right quantity ends up in clean, correctly labelled containers. An independent second check of each dispensed item and its quantity is required and must be documented. Everything dispensed for one batch is kept as a group and visibly labelled as belonging to that batch.
system_implications: Dispensing module: user must hold the 'dispenser' qualification (training record current) to log in to the booth; material lot scanned and checked against BOM, released status and retest/expiry date; weight captured directly from a calibrated, daily-checked balance with tolerance check against target; container label printed automatically. Independent check is either a second person e-signature (different user) or a validated system check (barcode + balance interface) documented as equivalent. Dispensed items grouped into a batch 'kit' with kit label and completeness check before issue to production. Injectables: also dispensing of WFI volumes, pH adjusters, filter/stopper components; tablets: API potency-adjusted quantities with compensating excipient.
verification_test: Log in without dispenser qualification -> refused. Scan wrong lot or a quarantined/expired lot -> refused. Weight outside tolerance cannot be confirmed. Verifier cannot be the dispenser. Kit cannot be issued with a missing component.

requirement: Cross-contamination must be prevented using quality risk management informed by toxicological assessment (health-based exposure limits); the QRM outcome decides whether premises/equipment must be dedicated and how extensive the technical measures (e.g. dedicated or self-contained areas, closed systems, barriers, validated cleaning) and organisational measures (e.g. campaigns, dedicated gowning, cleaning verification, status records) must be; the measures and their effectiveness are reviewed periodically. Non-medicinal products are normally kept out of medicinal production areas.
system_implications: Product master carries cross-contamination attributes (HBEL/PDE class, dedicated-equipment flag, allowed equipment/rooms, campaign rules, required cleaning procedure and verification type). Scheduler and execution enforce them: only permitted equipment/rooms selectable; campaign length and between-product cleaning type enforced; cleaning verification result (e.g. swab/rinse pass) must be recorded before a different product can use the equipment. Changeover matrix (product A -> product B) drives required cleaning level. Periodic review report of cleaning failures and changeovers.
verification_test: Assign a highly potent product to non-dedicated equipment not in its allowed list -> blocked. Attempt to start product B on equipment after product A with only a minor clean when the matrix requires full clean + verification -> blocked. Campaign exceeding configured maximum batches -> blocked or deviation required.

requirement: Packaging programmes must be planned to minimise risks of cross-contamination, mix-up or substitution; different products are not packaged close to each other unless physically segregated. The product name and batch number being packed must be displayed at every packaging station or line.
system_implications: Line/room model with segregation attributes; scheduler/execution refuses to start a second product on an adjacent line flagged as not physically segregated. Each line has an electronic line-status display (HMI/terminal/screen) driven by the active packaging order showing product, strength, pack, batch number and status; the display clears only when the order is closed and line clearance is done.
verification_test: Start product X on line 1; attempt product Y on non-segregated line 2 in the same room -> blocked. Line display shows current product/batch and reverts to 'awaiting clearance' at order close.

requirement: Before packaging starts, the work area, packaging lines, printers and other equipment must be verified clean and free of any product, material or document from earlier work that is not needed now; this line clearance follows an appropriate checklist.
system_implications: Packaging order has a mandatory first step 'line clearance' with a master-defined, line-specific checklist (each item individually confirmed, e.g. feeder hoppers, reject bins, printer ribbons/plates, vision-system recipe, floor/under-machine areas, documents removed). Design choice (not mandated by the text, but common inspector expectation for mix-up risk): performer + independent verifier signatures by two different users, verifier typically QA or supervisor. The system also checks electronically that the previous order on that line is closed and reconciled and that no components of another order remain allocated to the line. No packaging step, printer job or line start can be released until clearance is signed.
verification_test: Attempt to start the first packaging step with clearance unsigned or only single-signed (when dual is configured) -> blocked. Same user signing as performer and verifier -> refused. Previous order on the line not closed -> clearance cannot be completed.

requirement: On arrival at the packaging area, every product and packaging component must be checked to confirm the right quantity, the right identity and agreement with the packaging instructions.
system_implications: Receipt-at-line step: scan each bulk container and packaging component lot; system checks item code and artwork/version against the packaging master BOM, released status, expiry, and issued quantity vs. required quantity; mismatches block the step. Quantities received are posted to the reconciliation ledger for the order.
verification_test: Scan a carton of the wrong artwork version or a leaflet for another market -> rejected. Scan a quarantined component lot -> rejected. Received quantity feeds reconciliation.

requirement: Containers must be cleaned before they are filled, with particular care to prevent or remove foreign matter such as glass or metal particles. Labelling should normally follow filling and closing without delay; where it does not, procedures must prevent mix-ups and wrong labelling.
system_implications: Injectables edition (primary relevance): record container washing/depyrogenation and sterilisation status for each lot of vials/ampoules/stoppers with hold-time limits; unlabelled filled units (e.g. held for inspection before labelling) are tracked as 'bright stock' with unique tray/container IDs, location, count and hold-time; labelling order can only consume bright stock of the matching batch, verified by scan. Tablets edition: bottle cleaning/air-rinse and foreign-matter checks; bulk tablets in unlabelled containers carry system-printed identity labels. Maximum interval between filling and labelling configurable with alert.
verification_test: Attempt to label bright-stock trays from batch A under order for batch B -> rejected. Bright stock exceeding maximum unlabelled hold time raises an exception. Filling step blocked if container depyrogenation/sterile hold time has expired (injectables).

requirement: Printed components need special care: secure storage with access limited to authorised people; loose items such as cut labels kept and moved in closed, separate containers; and issue to production only by authorised staff following an approved written procedure. Each incoming lot of printed or primary packaging material is assigned its own reference number or identification mark. Primary or printed packaging that is out of date or obsolete must be destroyed, with the disposal documented.
system_implications: Packaging-material issue transaction restricted to an authorised role; each issued unit (reel, carton bundle, sealed box of cut labels) scanned by its internal lot/reference number and linked to the packaging order; closed-container ID recorded for cut labels. Artwork version lifecycle: when an artwork is superseded, all stock lots of the old version are automatically blocked for issue and routed to a destruction task requiring recorded, witnessed disposal.
verification_test: Non-authorised user attempts to issue labels -> refused. Issue of a lot whose artwork version is obsolete -> blocked. Destruction task for obsolete stock requires quantities, method, date and signatures and closes the lot.

requirement: Correct execution of every printing operation (e.g. batch code, expiry date), whether done separately or during packaging, must be checked and recorded, and any hand printing re-checked at regular intervals. Extra care is required with cut labels and with off-line overprinting; roll-fed labels are normally preferred over cut labels to help avoid mix-ups.
system_implications: Variable print data (batch, expiry, MFG date, serial/2D code, price where applicable) is sent electronically from the batch record to printers/coders (no manual keying); expiry is calculated from the master shelf-life rule. Start-of-run and periodic print verification step: operator/vision system confirms printed text against expected values; results recorded with specimen image. Configurable recurring re-check interval for any manual/hand printing. Master flags cut-label usage and off-line overprinting as higher-risk operations requiring additional controls (e.g. 100% vision check, dual verification).
verification_test: Batch data change after print setup -> printer job invalidated until re-verified. Start-up print check missing -> line cannot go to production mode. Hand-print re-check overdue -> alarm and exception entry.

requirement: The correct operation of electronic code readers, label counters and comparable devices must be checked. Printed or embossed information on packs must be clear and must not easily fade or rub off.
system_implications: Device challenge tests defined in the master (e.g. deliberately present wrong-code, missing-label, unreadable-code and missing-leaflet test pieces) at start-up, after interventions/stoppages, and at end of run; each challenge result is recorded (pass/fail, who, when) and a failed or missing challenge blocks production mode. Challenge test pieces are counted out and back in. Print quality check (grade for 2D codes where applicable, legibility, smudge/rub resistance per specification) recorded as an IPC.
verification_test: Skip the start-up challenge -> line cannot run in production mode. Record a failed challenge -> line stopped and deviation required. Challenge pieces not all returned at end -> reconciliation exception.

requirement: During packaging, on-line checks must at least confirm that finished packs look right and are complete, that the correct product and components are being used and any overprint is right, and that line monitoring devices are working. Units taken off the line as samples must never be put back.
system_implications: IPC plan in packaging master contains (as a minimum) these check categories at defined frequency with pass/fail and sample counts; missed IPCs raise alerts. Samples withdrawn are recorded by quantity and purpose and are automatically deducted in reconciliation; the system provides no transaction to return sampled units to the line. Injectables: also container-closure checks (crimp/seal), label placement on vials; tablets: blister seal integrity/leak test, count per bottle.
verification_test: IPC not recorded within its interval -> alert and exception report entry. Attempt to add sampled units back to good output -> not possible. Reconciliation shows sample quantities as a separate line.

requirement: If product is caught up in an unusual event (e.g. jam, spill, dropped units, suspected mix-up), it may re-enter the process only after it has been specially inspected, the event investigated, and authorised staff have approved; this must be documented in detail.
system_implications: 'Set-aside/unusual event' transaction: affected units are counted and moved to a quarantined set-aside bucket linked to an event record (what happened, time, quantity, location). Reintroduction requires inspection result entry, investigation reference and approval e-signature by an authorised role (not the operator); otherwise units go to reject. All quantities flow into reconciliation.
verification_test: Record a jam with 40 units set aside; attempt to add them back to good output without approval -> blocked. With inspection + approval, reintroduced quantity appears in the record and reconciliation with the event ID.

requirement: Any significant or unusual discrepancy found when reconciling bulk quantity and printed packaging materials against units produced must be investigated and satisfactorily explained before the batch is released.
system_implications: End-of-order reconciliation computed automatically per bulk lot and per printed component: issued = used + destroyed + returned + samples + rejects (+ set-aside), with master-defined limits (tighter, often zero-tolerance, for batch-coded printed items). Result outside limits forces a linked deviation/investigation; the order cannot be closed and the batch cannot be certified until the investigation is closed and approved by QA. Tablets: bulk tablets by weight/count vs. packs produced; injectables: filled/inspected units vs. labelled units vs. cartons.
verification_test: Enter counts leaving 12 labels unaccounted with a zero-tolerance limit -> order close blocked, deviation required; QP certification blocked until deviation closed. Counts within limits -> order closes normally.

requirement: When packaging is finished, any unused packaging material already coded with the batch must be destroyed and the destruction recorded; returning uncoded printed materials to stock must follow a documented procedure.
system_implications: Order close-out wizard: system distinguishes coded vs. uncoded leftovers (based on whether in-line/off-line coding occurred). Coded leftovers must be entered on a destruction record (quantity, method, witness) and can never be returned to stock; uncoded leftovers go through a return-to-stock transaction with count verification, re-labelling of the container and QA/stores acceptance, updating the component lot quantity.
verification_test: Attempt to return batch-coded cartons to stock -> no transaction available. Uncoded label return requires counted quantity, verification signature and updates stock. Destruction quantities appear in the reconciliation.

requirement: Necessary in-process and environmental controls must be performed and recorded, and intermediate and bulk products must be held under appropriate conditions.
system_implications: IPCs scheduled by the master (frequency, sample size, limits) with automatic data capture from instruments where possible (balances, hardness/thickness testers, checkweighers, fill-weight systems, pH/conductivity meters); out-of-limit results trigger defined reactions. Environmental data for the room during the step (e.g. temperature/RH for hygroscopic tablets; for injectables grade A/B particle counts, viable monitoring results, differential pressures) are linked to the batch record by time window from the monitoring system, and excursions are pulled into the exception report. Bulk/intermediate holds record container, location, storage condition and hold start/stop, with maximum hold time checks.
verification_test: Miss a scheduled IPC -> alert and exception. Inject an EM excursion during the filling window -> appears in batch exception report and blocks QA review completion until assessed. Bulk hold exceeding validated time -> blocked or deviation required.

requirement: Rejected materials and products must be clearly marked as rejected and segregated in restricted-access storage. Their fate (return to supplier, reprocessing where appropriate, or destruction) must be approved and documented by authorised people.
system_implications: 'Rejected' is a hard system status that blocks every consumption, issue, packaging and shipping transaction; rejected stock must be moved to a restricted location type. Disposition workflow (return to supplier / reprocess / destroy) with authorised-role approval e-signature and a record of the executed action and quantities. In-process rejects (e.g. tablets rejected by checkweigher, vials rejected at visual inspection) are counted into reject containers with IDs and follow the same disposition path.
verification_test: Try to dispense or package a rejected lot -> blocked. Attempt to move rejected stock to a normal location -> blocked. Disposition without authorised approval -> blocked; completed disposition visible in lot history.

requirement: Reprocessing of rejected product is to be exceptional: allowed only when final quality is unaffected, specifications are met, and it follows a defined, authorised procedure after risk evaluation; a record of the reprocessing must be kept.
system_implications: Reprocessing can only be executed from a pre-approved reprocessing master/procedure linked to the product (never ad hoc), launched from an approved deviation/change record with documented risk assessment. The reprocessing record is generated like a batch record, linked to the original batch genealogy, and flagged so QA/QP see it at release; additional testing requirements from the procedure are enforced. Injectables: reprocessing is often not permitted for sterile products (e.g. re-filtration only if validated/registered) - system allows reprocessing masters to be disabled per product.
verification_test: Attempt to start reprocessing without an approved reprocessing procedure and approved risk assessment -> blocked. Completed reprocessing appears in the original batch genealogy and QP review flags.

requirement: Adding all or part of earlier batches that meet quality requirements into a later batch of the same product, at a defined manufacturing stage, needs prior authorisation, must follow a defined procedure after assessing risks (including any effect on shelf life), and must be recorded. QC must decide whether reprocessed product, or product containing recovered material, needs extra testing.
system_implications: Recovered-material addition is a specific step type available only where the master defines it (stage, maximum proportion, eligible source batches). Source batch must be same product, conforming status and within age limits; pre-authorisation e-signature required; genealogy records source batch IDs and quantities; expiry of the receiving batch is calculated from the oldest contributing batch where the procedure requires. QC additional-testing decision is captured as a mandatory field before release.
verification_test: Try to add material from a different product or a non-conforming batch -> blocked. Add eligible recovered material: pre-authorisation required, genealogy and expiry calculation updated, QC decision field mandatory before release.

requirement: Market returns that have been outside the manufacturer's control default to destruction unless their quality is not in doubt. Resale, relabelling or use in a later batch is allowed only after QC has critically assessed them under a written procedure, considering the product type, any special storage needs, its condition and history, and how long it has been out. If quality is doubtful the goods must not be reissued or reused (though basic chemical recovery of the active substance may be possible). All actions must be recorded.
system_implications: Returned-goods receipt creates a quarantined 'returned' lot linked to the original batch; disposition requires a QC assessment form (storage history incl. cold chain for injectables, condition, time since shipment) and QC e-signature; default disposition is destroy. Returned units cannot be consumed as recovered material or repackaged unless the assessment result permits it, and the resulting action is recorded against the original batch history.
verification_test: Try to repackage returned units without a QC assessment -> blocked. Assessment 'doubt' -> only destruction (or chemical recovery route) available.

requirement: Finished products stay in quarantine, under manufacturer-defined conditions, until final release (evaluation per Chapter 6 and QP certification); only after release do they become usable stock. Incoming materials and products are likewise held in physical or administrative quarantine until released.
system_implications: Every produced lot is created in 'Quarantine' status; status change to 'Released' is possible only via the QP certification transaction after batch record review is complete (all steps signed, deviations closed, reconciliation passed, lab results approved). Interfaces to ERP/WMS must respect the status (no shipment of quarantined stock). Administrative quarantine is acceptable if enforced electronically.
verification_test: Attempt to ship or allocate a quarantined finished lot via ERP interface -> rejected. QP certification button disabled while any release prerequisite is open. Status history shows who released and when.

requirement: Products and materials need protection against microbial and other contamination throughout processing; handling of dry materials requires special measures to stop dust being generated and spread, especially for highly hazardous or sensitising substances.
system_implications: Tablets edition: master can require dust-control prerequisites before open handling steps (e.g. local exhaust/containment verified on, room pressure cascade OK, contained transfer system connected) captured as signed checks or interface signals; weighing/dispensing of potent APIs only in designated booths. Injectables edition: aseptic-processing prerequisites before exposure steps (grade A airflow/particle status OK, sterile equipment within hold time, gowning qualification valid, interventions logged); microbial hold-time limits for non-sterile bulk solution before sterile filtration (bioburden sample recorded).
verification_test: Attempt to start an open-powder step while the containment/extraction check is not recorded -> blocked (tablets). Attempt to start filling with sterile-hold expired on filling parts or with an active grade A alarm -> blocked (injectables). Bulk solution time from compounding start to filtration exceeding limit -> deviation required.

requirement: Checks must confirm that pipelines and other equipment that transfer product from one area to another are correctly connected.
system_implications: Transfer steps (e.g. bulk solution from compounding vessel to filling line through transfer panel/hoses; vacuum/pneumatic powder transfer to tablet press hopper) include a connection-verification step: scan of source vessel, transfer panel/hose/port and destination IDs, or signal from panel proximity sensors, compared to the master route; mismatch blocks the transfer. Result recorded with performer and verifier.
verification_test: Scan a hose connected to the wrong destination vessel -> transfer blocked. Correct route scan -> transfer enabled and recorded.

requirement: Storage labels on starting materials must identify the material and its receipt lot, and show QC status and any expiry or retest date where relevant; with a fully computerised storage system this may be held electronically instead of legibly on the label. Measures must assure the identity of the contents of every container, and only materials released by QC and still within their retest date may be used.
system_implications: eBMR relies on (or provides) a validated inventory status as the master for material status; at dispensing and at charging into equipment, each container scan checks identity (item code), released status, retest/expiry date, and container-level identity confirmation where required (e.g. per-container ID test status). If labels carry only a barcode, the system is the authoritative source and must be validated for that purpose.
verification_test: Scan a container whose lot is 'on test', rejected, past retest date, or whose container identity test is pending -> blocked at dispensing and at charging. Released, in-date container -> accepted.

requirement: Production must be carried out and overseen by competent staff, and every handling activity for materials and products, from goods receipt through processing and packaging to distribution, must follow written procedures or instructions and be recorded where necessary.
system_implications: Each master step declares the qualification/training required (per procedure version); the system checks the user's current training status (from LMS interface or internal records) before allowing them to perform or verify the step, and blocks users whose training is missing or expired. Supervisor/verifier roles are distinct permissions. Each step links to the governing procedure/instruction version.
verification_test: User trained on SOP v3 attempts a step now requiring SOP v4 training -> refused. Qualified user can perform; verifier role cannot be assigned to an untrained user.

requirement: New formulas or methods of preparation must be shown suitable for routine production, significant changes to the process (including equipment or material changes) that may affect quality or reproducibility must be validated, and processes are periodically reassessed; validation results are recorded.
system_implications: Master recipe change control: every master change is classified (editorial vs. process-impacting); process-impacting changes (CPP ranges, equipment class, materials/suppliers, batch size, sequence) require a linked change-control and validation reference before approval. Masters carry a validation-status attribute; batches produced under a master pending validation (e.g. PPQ batches) are flagged so release requires the validation outcome. Master comparison report (diff) supports the assessment.
verification_test: Attempt to approve a master revision with a changed CPP range and no change-control/validation link -> blocked. Diff report lists changed fields. PPQ-flagged batch cannot be certified without validation outcome entry.

requirement: The manufacturer must promptly tell the marketing authorisation holder about manufacturing constraints that could cause an abnormal restriction of supply, so the MAH can notify the competent authorities.
system_implications: Peripheral to the batch record but can be supported: batch/campaign rejection, prolonged line holds, or major deviations flagged with a 'potential supply impact' attribute that generates a notification task to the supply/QA contact for the MAH, with timestamped acknowledgement.
verification_test: Reject a batch flagged 'supply impact' -> notification task created with due date and audit trail of acknowledgement.

text: Source access: health.ec.europa.eu, ema.europa.eu and picscheme.org were blocked by this environment's network policy, so no primary PDF was opened. Clause content was cross-checked via web-search summaries. Before design sign-off, check against the PDFs: Chapter 5 clause numbers 5.13, 5.22, 5.32-5.34, 5.49, 5.51, 5.63-5.65 and 5.69 (from recollection of the 2014 text; the search tool gave conflicting numbers for the packaging clauses), and the draft Chapter 4 clause numbers other than 4.10-4.18, 4.12 and 4.13.

Final status of revised Chapter 4 (and Annex 11 / new Annex 22): the latest source found (hero.ie, citing the EudraLex page as of 30 July 2026) says they were still drafts. Nothing found shows publication between August and 27 September 2026. Re-check the EudraLex Vol.4 page. Once final, confirm (a) the operative date and transition period, (b) whether batch processing/packaging record content lists or batch retention periods changed, and (c) the final wording on hybrid records and printing electronic records for handwritten signature.

Line clearance sign-off: Chapter 5 (5.50) requires line clearance against a checklist but does not itself require two people. Is dual sign-off (operator plus independent QA/supervisor) a product default, or configurable per site and line? Recommendation: default ON for packaging, configurable for processing, because 5.50 (see EU5-09) plus inspection practice treat mix-ups as high risk.

Chapter 4 4.17 asks for an approved formula per batch size. QA/regulatory must decide whether one master approved for a validated batch-size range (scaled at batch creation) is acceptable, or whether each discrete batch size needs its own approved master. The answer changes the master data model.

Chapter 4 4.21(h) lets reconciliation be omitted where 'robust electronic controls' exist, but gives no definition. The criteria must be defined (e.g. 100% vision verification with confirmed reject, roll-fed labels, serialization aggregation) and the approval route for switching reconciliation off per component.

Review by exception (Chapter 4, note to 4.20) only covers validated processes that are continuously monitored and controlled. It is unclear how far it may reach for manual steps, which are common in tablet granulation and in aseptic interventions for injectables. The review-by-exception scope should be aligned with the draft Chapter 4 data-criticality model and with the Annex 11 audit-trail review expectations, which are researched separately.

Injectables edition: 5.67 allows reprocessing of rejected product only as an exception. Confirm product by product whether any reprocessing (e.g. re-filtration or re-inspection) is registered in the MA. The default for sterile products should be 'reprocessing disabled'. Also check the Annex 1 (2022) requirements that interact with Chapter 5 clauses 5.10, 5.53 and 5.54; these are out of scope here.

requirement: Consolidated signature points in the in-force Chapter 4: authorised persons approve, sign and date instruction documents; alterations are signed and dated; batch processing and packaging records identify who performed each significant step and, where relevant, who checked it; departures from instructions carry a signed authorisation; and the person responsible for processing or packaging approves the completed record. The 2011 chapter does not describe how electronic signatures work; that comes from Annex 11 (section 14, 2011), which was not re-checked in this task.
system_implications: Signature catalogue built into the product with one configurable signature type per point: master approval, correction, step performed, step verified, deviation authorisation, production/packaging record approval, QA review, QP certification. Each type defines the allowed roles, whether the signer must differ from earlier signers on the same object, and whether re-authentication is needed. Every signature event is recorded in the audit trail and shown in the rendered record.
verification_test: For each signature type, test: correct role accepted, wrong role refused, the same person refused where independence is required, and the signature (name, date-time, meaning) appears in the rendered batch record and audit trail.

requirement: In the chapter, 'written' covers data recorded on any medium, provided it can be rendered in human-readable form. Records must give the history of each manufactured batch, including its distribution. Controls must keep documents accurate, intact, available and legible.
system_implications: Every electronic batch record, including its metadata, attachments and audit trail, can be rendered on demand as a complete human-readable report (screen and PDF/print) for inspectors and the QP, for the whole retention period. The batch genealogy can be linked to distribution data held in ERP, so the history of a batch can be traced forward to customers for recall.
verification_test: Render an archived batch record: every step, value, signature, comment, deviation link and audit-trail entry is present and legible. From a finished batch ID, a forward trace returns its distribution records.
